case_title: State of Karnataka v. Selvi J. Jayalalitha & Ors.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.109; PC Act s.13(1)(e), s.13(2), s.5(1)(e); Code of Criminal Procedure s.452
aggravating_circumstances: Conspiracy, disproportionate assets, benami transactions, active abetment
offence_finally_established: Criminal misconduct under s.13(1)(e) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that the accused, including a public servant, entered into a conspiracy to acquire and hold disproportionate assets through shell companies and benami transactions. The accused dispersed assets in the names of others and engaged in financial transactions that indicated active abetment and conspiracy. The trial court found that the accused had executed a power of attorney, established firms during the check period, and engaged in financial transactions that demonstrated collective culpability. The High Court partially reversed these findings, but the Supreme Court restored the trial court's conviction, finding the evidence of conspiracy and abetment overwhelming.
